title: The control-plane doc promises an expired_request tombstone and result pruning that the code does not implement
outcome: docs/features/behavioral-control-plane.md's "Crash, restart, and replay" section matches the shipped control runtime: what an exact retry returns, what happens with no stored result (ControlTurnGrantNotFound), which refusal codes an expired unbegun grant can produce, what a new host connection invalidates, and that no request-key tombstone or result pruning exists today (or it is marked as designed, not built). A host implementer reading it can't rely on behaviour that isn't there.
acceptance: behavioral-control-plane.md:1262-1281 states only shipped behaviour, with any designed-but-unbuilt part (the expired_request tombstone, grant and result pruning) explicitly marked as not built, consistent with docs/shipped.md.

The section states that an expired unbegun grant is refused with grant_scope_mismatch or grant_expired depending on whether it was already expired by a status read or resume, that a new HostControlServer connection expires all issued grants for the session while begun turns survive, and that session_status lazily expires issued grants.
